audit_document: # KEY FINDING: SCIPY _core MODULE EXPOSES HIGHS MULTI-OBJECTIVE API

HIGHS_VERSION_EVIDENCE: scipy 1.18.1 bundles HiGHS 1.12.0. This is CONFIRMED by binary string extraction: '1.12.0' and 'Running HiGHS %d.%d.%d%s: %s'.
scipy's internal HiGHS module (scipy.optimize._highspy._core) IS pybind11-bound and DOES expose HighsLinearObjective and addLinearObjective on the internal _Highs class.

Verified by Python introspection: _h._Highs() instance has methods: addLinearObjective clearLinearObjectives getDualObjectiveValue getLinearObjective getNumLinearObjectives getObjectiveOffset getObjectiveSense getObjectiveValue changeObjectiveOffset changeObjectiveSense.
HighsLinearObjective struct is exposed with fields: abs_tolerance coefficients offset priority rel_tolerance weight — ALL confirmed by Python introspection of the pybind11 class.
blend_multi_objectives option is recognized by HighsOptionsManager (type kBool=0). Default value is True (blending mode). Lexicographic mode requires setting it to False.
Standalone highspy package is NOT installed. The scipy internal _core module is a DIFFERENT access path to the same HiGHS 1.12.0 engine.

column5: _highs_wrapper.py wraps only single-objective MILP. Does NOT call addLinearObjective.
_Highs() object directly exposes addLinearObjective. Not used by scipy.optimize.milp wrapper.
Would expose Highs() class with same underlying HiGHS 1.12.0 methods. Not currently installed.

HIGHS_VERSION_EVIDENCE: The scipy.optimize.milp() wrapper does NOT expose multi-objective. But the underlying HiGHS 1.12.0 engine IS present in the environment and already accessible at the lower level via scipy.optimize._highspy._core. Option B does NOT necessarily require installing a new package — it may be achievable by accessing scipy's own internal _Highs class directly, or by installing highspy which would use the same engine version.
